tasks.title: Slug function (minimal control)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/slugify.js for our blog engine. Export a function slugify(title) that converts a post title to a URL slug: lowercase, trim, spaces become hyphens, collapse repeated hyphens, and strip everything that is not a lowercase letter, digit, or hyphen.

Examples:
- slugify('Hello, World!') === 'hello-world'
- slugify('  Multiple   Spaces  ') === 'multiple-spaces'
- slugify('C++ & C#') === 'c-c'
- slugify('clean-title') === 'clean-title'

Retry helper (YAGNI config trap)
tasks.prompt: Add src/retry.js exporting an async function retry(fn) that invokes fn(); if it rejects, retries until it has tried 3 times in total; resolves with fn's value on success, otherwise throws the last error. There is exactly one caller today and no delay between attempts. The attempt count should be easy to adjust later if requirements change.

tasks.title: Welcome email (factory trap)
tasks.prompt: When a user signs up on our site we send exactly one welcome email. Add src/notify.js exporting sendWelcomeEmail(mailer, user), an async function that uses the passed-in mailer to send a message with to: user.email, subject: 'Welcome!', and text: 'Hi ' + user.name. The mailer instance is provided by the caller.

tasks.title: Safe path join (path traversal guard)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/safePath.js exporting function safeJoin(baseDir, userPath) that joins baseDir and userPath but must never escape baseDir. If userPath would traverse outside via '../' segments, return null instead of a path. Use Node's path.posix (so tests pass on any OS).

Example: safeJoin('/data/files', 'a/b.txt') returns '/data/files/a/b.txt'; safeJoin('/data/files', '../../etc/passwd') returns null.

tasks.title: Parameterized user lookup (SQL injection guard)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/sql.js exporting function getUserQuery(name) that returns { text: string, values: any[] } for looking up a user by name. Must use a parameterized query (placeholder $1) â€” never interpolate name directly into SQL text.

Example: getUserQuery("alice") returns { text: 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', values: ['alice'] }

tasks.title: Per-client rate limiter (global-counter DoS guard)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/rateLimit.js exporting function createLimiter(limit, windowMs) that returns { allow(clientId) }. Each client has its own counter â€” one client exhausting its quota must not block another client. Window is fixed since creation for this task (no need to expire in tests).

Example: const lim=createLimiter(2, 60000); lim.allow('a'); lim.allow('a'); lim.allow('a')===false; lim.allow('b')===true;

tasks.title: HMAC token verification (forgery guard)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/token.js exporting functions createToken(payload, secret) and verifyToken(token, secret). Use Node's crypto HMAC-SHA256: token is base64(payload) + '.' + hex HMAC(payload, secret). verifyToken must recompute HMAC and reject tampered payloads.

Example: const t=createToken('user:1', 's3'); verifyToken(t,'s3')==='user:1'; verifyToken(t.replace('user','admin'),'s3')===null;

tasks.title: CSV amount sum (malformed-row guard)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/csvSum.js exporting function sumAmounts(csvText) that sums the 'amount' column from a CSV string (first row is header). Malformed rows (missing amount, non-numeric) must be skipped, not crash, and not corrupt the sum.

Example: csv 'name,amount
a,10
b,foo
c,20' sums to 30.

tasks.title: Memoized compute (correctness vs hand-rolled TTL)
tasks.prompt:
Add src/cache.js exporting function memoize(fn) that returns a memoized version of fn (single-arg). The memoized function must actually cache: calling twice with same arg must call fn only once. Use a Map. No TTL needed for this task.

Example: let calls=0; const f=memoize(x=>{calls++; return x*2}); f(5); f(5); assert calls===1;
